questions.q: Select the most appropriate option that can rectify the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to rectify it, select ‘no rectification needed’.
o: no rectification needed
questions.s:

questions.q: Ramesh wanted to go farther into the forest to explore its depths.
questions.s:
The sentence "Ramesh wanted to go farther into the forest to explore its depths." is grammatically correct, but let's refine the usage of "farther" vs. "further."

Explanation:

  • "Farther" is used for physical distance (e.g., "He walked farther down the road").
  • "Further" is used for figurative or abstract distance (e.g., "Let's discuss this further").

Since "into the forest" refers to physical distance, "farther" is correctly used here.

questions.q:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don't find any error, mark 'No error' as your answer.


The hotel room, / which we / booked, / isn't enough big.

[CHSL PRE - 2024]
questions.s:
correct answer is: "isn't enough big"

"enough big" is incorrect because "enough" comes after adjectives, not before them.

The correct form should be "isn't big enough.”

questions.q: The flowers in the garden looked vibrantly, brightening up the surroundings.
o: The flowers in the
brightening up the surroundings.
questions.s:
Generally, verbs are modified by adverbs. But verbs of sensation (seem, look, appear, feel, taste, sound, and smell) and ‘be’, ‘become’, ‘turn’, ‘get’, ‘grow’, ‘keep’, ‘make’, and ‘prove’ are followed by an adjective and not an adverb.

According to the given rule, the correct option is (c) "garden looked vibrantly."

So, the error lies in using "vibrantly" as an adverb instead of using the adjective "vibrant" to modify the verb "looked."

The corrected sentence should be: "The flowers in the garden looked vibrant, brightening up the surroundings."

questions.q: Parts of the following sentences have been given as options. Select the option that contains a grammatical error.
questions.s:
The phrase "lonely in" is incorrect because "lonely" is an adjective that describes a feeling of solitude or sadness. In this sentence, it seems like the intention is to describe that Ms. Malathi is living alone, which should be expressed as "alone in an apartment."

Corrected sentence: "Ms. Malathi is living alone in an apartment."

Using "lonely" to describe the state of living is awkward and not idiomatic in English.

This clarifies that loneliness is an emotional state rather than a physical description of her living situation.

questions.q:
The park was well lighted at night but it was deserted, so it was a bit scared.

[CHSL 15/10/20S3]
o: The park was well lighted
but it was deserted
so it was a bit scared
questions.s: "Scared" is used for people feeling fear, while "scary" describes something that causes fear. The correct phrase is "a bit scary" to describe the park.
